primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators IV
primary_antecedent.scope: Complete prescribed finite concave-index realization, exact homogeneous equation, full positive-ray wavefront equality and all affine packet norm calculations. The direct positive-series argument supplies the simultaneous construction.

source_correspondence: The complete statement permits every finite nonincreasing concave function on the whole real line when Q has a positive value, and every finite concave function when Q is indefinite. The exact homogeneous equation and full positive-ray wavefront equality are retained.

Ordered secant inequalities prove local Lipschitz bounds and finite one-sided slopes. Rational-point supporting lines majorize the function globally and have precisely its infimum, including corners and unbounded slopes at infinity.

The logarithmically shifted packet has a smooth nonnegative partial Fourier amplitude. Its exact equation has the correct sign for D=-i partial. The quadratic phase splits into c log(lambda) plus uniformly bounded terms on each compact time interval.

Both frequency chain rules, all repeated derivatives, time derivatives and logarithmic losses are proved. Every affine majorant satisfies one common amplitude order on each time compact, independently of the derivative order; only constants vary.

The inverse Fourier integral defines an actual distribution with finite test bounds. Full frequency integration by parts gives smooth tails away from the spatial origin, rapidly decreasing with all derivatives on every compact time interval.

Complementary angular estimates and time integration give rapid decay outside every neighborhood of the full positive last covector. The cutoff-convolution proof retains polynomial tails and proves the actual wavefront containment.

For every real Sobolev order, including negative ones, the full Fourier norm is equivalent in finiteness to the partial weighted energy. Time Plancherel and Tonelli apply before the possibly infinite frequency integral. Exact angular localization and Schwartz spatial tails make this a genuine microlocal criterion.
The full transverse Jacobian is (lambda/log(lambda))^((n-2)/2). Strict convergence and divergence give the exact affine index -b-ct-n/4; logarithms are retained to determine endpoint attainment.
A countable list includes common-order derivative bounds, all complementary cones and every strict rational local weighted energy. Each affine packet has finite values for all tests.

Strictly positive diagonal coefficients make the series converge in every listed seminorm. Uniform derivative limits and complete weighted L2 limits are identified with the same amplitude. The exact PDE survives differentiation and inverse transformation, with no forcing error.

The summed energies prove every order below the target index. Pointwise positivity bounds each energy below by every positive packet contribution, enforcing every affine upper obstruction with no cancellation. Finite indices give equality of the full wavefront set at every time.

Three complete solutions verify the n/4 shift and logarithmic endpoint, a nonincreasing corner, and a two-sided indefinite corner. The sign explanation uses the ordinary estimate after reversing time, without assuming the central line belongs to N11.

The positive series realizes the prescribed index and solves the model equation exactly; necessity of concavity for arbitrary solutions is a separate theorem. The complex-cutoff energy theorem treats a different measurement problem. The monotonicity argument here uses ordinary sign propagation without assuming that the model curve lies in N11.
